skills: Year 1
Reading a statute section by section - operative words, provisos, explanations, illustrations - from the first week of LAW 102 Obligations: Contract Law and LAW 103 Delict: Law of Tort.
Briefing a case on half a page (facts, issue, holding, ratio) and a case bank started in LAW 101 Legal Concepts of Jurisprudence and LAW 202 Muslim Family Law and Reforms.
Legal English that is plain and exact: ENG 101 and the 2nd Semester English slot, used on every answer you write.
The first chains cleared first time: LAW 102 opens LAW 201 and LAW 203; LAW 202 opens LAW 104 Constitutional Law.
Year 2
The Residential Semester (the 3rd Semester, at Savar) done with its compulsory Gen-Ed courses and no LAW course pending.
Problem questions answered by method - IRAC - in LAW 205 Business Law, LAW 301 Agricultural Law and Reforms and LAW 302 Criminal Law.
Sections tied to leading cases across the doctrinal core (LAW 104, LAW 201, LAW 203, LAW 204).
Speaking on your feet: class presentations, the Debating Club, a first intra-moot with the School's Moot Court Society.
Year 3
Company, insurance, tax and intellectual property learned as one commercial set (LAW 303, LAW 307, LAW 434, LAW 322) - in the 7-course semester the plan prints.
Procedure as a sequence you can draw (LAW 305 Principles of Civil Procedure, LAW 308 Criminal Procedures) and evidence as rules you can apply (LAW 306).
Public international law and its branches (LAW 304, then LAW 346 Environmental Law, LAW 342 Legal Systems and Institutions, LAW 447 Human Rights).
A memorial researched and written with a team; a court visited on your own initiative and written up.
Year 4
Drafting: deeds, notices, petitions and the documents of civil litigation (LAW 401 Conveyancing and Legal Writings, LAW 403 Moot-Court Sessions).
LAW 402 Legal Research and Methodology [Dissertation Paper]: abstract, proposal and final thesis, each presented as the page says they are assessed.
ADR and arbitration (LAW 344), cyber law (LAW 425) and the personal-law set (LAW 351, LAW 352, LAW 404) explained in words a client would follow.
A plan for the year after graduation - chambers, examinations or an LL.M. - lined up a semester early, with the Law Alumni Association (LAABRACU) as a first contact.
dept.career_intro: The programme page names 'careers in the government, judicial service, business', 'Practising law as advocates at district/supreme courts' and 'Joining the judiciary as judges', with support from OCSAR and the Law Alumni Association of BRAC University (LAABRACU). Each door asks for different preparation from the 3rd year on, so let your 3rd and 4th-year courses, your moots and LAW 402 point the same way. These are common directions, not BRACU rules.

Government and public service

LAW 104 Constitutional Law, LAW 448 Administrative Law, LAW 302 Criminal Law; broad examination preparation alongside the degree.
Human rights, NGOs and international organisations
Legal aid, research, advocacy and programme work.
LAW 447 Human Rights, LAW 304 International Law [Public], LAW 345 Women, Law and Legal Protection, LAW 346 Environmental Law; report writing; an article in the Law Club newsletter 'Acumen'.
Property, succession and conveyancing practice
Deeds, registration, land and family matters - a large share of district practice.

LAW 203 Property Law and Transfer, LAW 204 Law of Registration and Limitation, LAW 401 Conveyancing and Legal Writings, LAW 202, LAW 351 Hindu Law and Succession, LAW 352, LAW 404 Law of Trusts and Codicils.

Cyber, data and intellectual-property work in companies and firms.
LAW 425 Cyber Law, LAW 322 Intellectual Property Law, LAW 344 ADR and Arbitration; one piece of writing on a live problem.

An LL.M. (the School of Law page links its own LLM programme), then research and teaching.

book.text: Read this first

This planner puts your whole Law degree in one place: every published course, the rules that move your CGPA, the dates that cost money, and a working page for every week of the semester - on your phone, offline, with the arithmetic done for you.
What you are holding

items: **Degree** - the Bachelor of Laws (LL.B. Hons.) as BRACU prints it: every course, its credits and its prerequisite. Pick a semester and a grade per course and the CGPA, the credit map, the Ready / Locked checks and your semester-by-semester plan follow.
**CGPA** - the grading scale, a quick semester GPA, what it takes to reach a target, a retake what-if on BRACU's own rule, and the CGPA lines that decide waivers and standing.
**Money** - this semester's bill at the published rates, the whole degree roughly, and the dates that cost money with a countdown you can send to your calendar.
**Semester** - deadlines and tasks, your routine with a clash check, and the working pages of a semester (set-up, course pages, check-ins, finals plan), one set per semester.
**Toolkit** - the tools this department's work actually needs, with logs and calculators that count and flag as you type.
**Rules** - BRACU's own grading, retake, probation, load, scholarship and fee rules, with the source named under each.
**More** - clubs and careers, the printable pages, an assignment cover page, the Excel version of the tracker, and your backup.

book.text: What it is not

items: It is **not an official BRACU document**. Nobody at the university wrote, checked or approved it.
It does **not replace your advisor**, your advising sheet or the student portal. Those decide what counts toward your degree.

It is **a snapshot**. Course lists, fees, CGPA lines and dates were read from BRACU's own web pages on 20 October 2026. Universities change these. When a notice and this planner disagree - cross the old line out here, and the notice wins.

book.text: Start in 15 minutes

items: On **Home**, type your name, the semester you were admitted in and the semester you are in now.
On **Degree**, pick the semester and the grade of every course you have passed. Your CGPA appears at once, and every course shows Ready, Locked or Open.
On **Money**, type this semester's fee and drop dates from the Registrar's calendar; they count down on Home.
On **Semester**, put your sections into the routine and your deadlines into the task list.
Open the **Toolkit** when the work starts: labs, projects, cases, the final-year runway.

book.text: Your data

Everything you type stays in this browser on this device - nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account and no internet is needed. That also means a cleared browser or a new phone starts empty. So, now and then, open **More** and tap **Save this planner with my data inside**: you get this same file back with everything you have typed written into it. Keep that copy - open it on a laptop, send it to a new phone, or hand it to next semester's you.

If a browser refuses to keep your data between visits (some phones open files in a way that forgets), Home tells you so and offers the same button. Your planner is then simply the latest copy you saved.

the Rules tab - Rules that move your CGPA and your money

Most students learn these rules by breaking one. Read them once now. Everything here is taken from BRAC University's published pages as they stood in October 2026; the source is named under each section.
The grading scale
BRAC University's undergraduate scale, in force since Fall 2020. Both A+ and A carry the full 4.0.
A+ to D- are passing grades. F is failing: it earns no credit and counts as zero in your GPA.
How your GPA and CGPA are worked out

Every course gives you **quality points = credits x grade point**. Add the quality points for a semester and divide by the credits you attempted for a letter grade: that is your semester GPA. Do the same across all semesters and you have your CGPA. The policy page prints the same formula: the sum of (grade points x credits) over the credits attempted.
Three things students get wrong

items: **An F stays in the sum until it is retaken.** It adds credits to the bottom of the fraction and nothing to the top.
**A D- passes, but it costs you.** A 3-credit D- is 2.1 quality points against 12.0 for an A - and a grade of B- or below is what the repeat rule exists for.
**W, I, P and AU never enter the GPA.** A W costs you the fee and the semester's work, not grade points.

book.text: How to read a section

items: **Place it.** Which Part and Chapter of the Act, and what the heading promises.
**Definitions first.** Find every defined term in the interpretation section before you read the operative words.
**The operative words.** Who may or must do what, to whom, on what conditions - break the sentence into its elements and number them.
**Then the qualifiers.** Provisos narrow the rule; exceptions take cases out of it; explanations settle a doubt; illustrations show the rule in action and are examples, not the rule.
**Linked sections.** What it refers to, and what refers back to it.
**The leading case** on the section - into the case bank, with its ratio.
**Amendments.** Confirm you have the current text; a bare Act printed years ago may not be. The Government's online Laws of Bangladesh database (bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd) carries consolidated Acts.

6. Moot court: LAW 403 and the Moot Court Society

**LAW 403 Moot-Court Sessions** is an 8th-Semester course (3 credits; prerequisites LAW 305 Principles of Civil Procedure and LAW 308 Criminal Procedures), assessed - in the page's words - by 'Drafting of various documents of civil litigation and actual participation in mock trial', in the campus's 'specially designed courtroom for moot-court session'. Outside the course, the School's Moot Court Society prepares teams for competitions: the School of Law page records success in national and international competitions including the ICRC Henry Dunant Moot Court Competitions, and in May 2026 the School hosted the IDLO-BRAC University Health Law Intra Moot Competition. book.text: Civil-litigation drafting set
LAW 403 is assessed on drafting, and LAW 401 Conveyancing and Legal Writings is drafting by definition. Whatever the document, the same checks apply before it leaves your hands:

items: Heading: the court, the case type or number, the parties with their descriptions - in the form the Code and the court's rules prescribe.
Facts in numbered paragraphs, in date order, one fact per paragraph, nothing argued yet.
The cause of action or ground, with the provision it rests on; jurisdiction and limitation stated and shown, not assumed.
The relief or prayer: specific, complete, with alternatives, and nothing the facts do not support.
Verification, affidavit, signature, date and the list of annexures, as the form requires.
Read it once as the opposing lawyer and once as the judge before you file it.

I address the bench correctly, stop when a question comes, answer it first and only then return to my road map.
I know my time limit and what I will cut if the bench takes my time.
